text: dsh-ui-font 是为 DSH 网页客户端增加字体自定义能力的插件。它在“设置 → 常规”中提供正文界面字体和代码等宽字体两项设置，让用户通过本机字体选择器添加字体，并调整回退顺序或移除字体。设置会保存到当前配置档案，主机端在页面首次呈现时注入字体样式，浏览器端也会同步更新样式。字体栈经过清理并在空值时回到默认值，适合希望调整阅读界面、代码块或本地化字体显示的 DSH Web 用户。安装并使用 DSH Web 即可，不需要额外的密钥或外部服务。

dsh-ui-font customizes fonts in the DSH web client. It adds separate settings for interface and code fonts. Pick installed families, reorder fallbacks, or remove them. Changes save to the profile and apply through page styles. Empty values use defaults; no API key or external service is needed.

dsh-ui-font 的功能「正文与代码字体设置」：在设置常规页提供两条字体栈设置，分别控制界面正文和代码等宽文字。用户可在本机字体列表中搜索并添加字体，也可调整顺序或移除。
dsh-ui-font 的功能「即时应用字体」：主机端把当前配置写入页面样式注入，浏览器端订阅设置并维护样式标签；修改字体后用于更新界面和代码的字体变量。
dsh-ui-font 的功能「字体栈清理与回退」：保存前将字体名称整理为 CSS 字体列表，去掉重复和空项；不安全字符会被清理，空值则恢复随附的默认字体栈。

dsh-ui-font README · dsh-ui-font：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI plugin that sets the UI and code font families from **Settings → General**.

[日本語](README.ja.md)

dsh-ui-font README · Why this exists：The DSH Web GUI exposes the colour scheme and the conversation font size in **Settings → General**, but not the font family. `dsh-client-ui-theme` ships `base.css` with two hardcoded stacks:

| Token | Used by | Stock value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dsw-font-family` | body text and UI chrome | `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", ...` |
| `--dsw-font-mono`, `--ds-font-family-code` | code blocks and monospace UI | `"SF Mono", "JetBrains Mono", "Fira Code", Consolas, ...` |

dsh-ui-font README · Why this exists：This plugin adds two rows to that settings page, stores the chosen stacks in its own profile entry, and applies them without touching any file inside the DSH installation (an npm update cannot revert them).

dsh-ui-font README · Install：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ui-font
dsh web
```

`dsh plugin` installs the package into the profile and appends dependency packages that declare `dsh.bundle` to `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically, so no manual patch editing is required.

A running `dsh web` composes `dsh.profile.bundles` once at startup and only watches the user patch layer (`cordis.patch.yml`), so **restart it after installing** — a browser refresh alone will not load the plugin.
dsh-ui-font README · Install：Uninstall with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-ui-font`.

dsh-ui-font README · Configure：Open **Settings → General**. Each row lists the saved families as ordered chips, shows a sample line set in that stack, and carries an **Add font** button:

| Row | Setting | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body font | `sans` | body text and UI chrome |
| Code font | `mono` | code blocks and monospaced text |

dsh-ui-font README · Configure：**Add font** opens a searchable list of the families installed on this machine, read with the browser's `queryLocalFonts()`, and each entry is rendered in its own face. Chrome asks for font access the first time; entries already in the stack carry a check mark, and picking one appends it to the end. The panel stays open so several families can be added in a row. When the browser cannot list local fonts, or you decline the prompt, the list falls back to a short set of common families and says so. A search term that matches nothing in the list offers `Add "<name>"`, so any family the browser can resolve stays reachable.

dsh-ui-font README · Configure：Each chip carries three buttons: move earlier, move later, and remove. The order is the fallback order, so keep a CJK-capable family after the Latin one. Every change saves immediately, and an unchanged stack writes nothing.

dsh-ui-font README · Configure：The stored value is still a plain CSS `font-family` list, so a hand edit works too. Braces, semicolons, and angle brackets are sanitised away, because the value is interpolated into a stylesheet. The two fields are declared `volatile()` in the plugin's schema, which is what makes them editable; a write lands in this plugin's entry inside the active profile patch, and only the fields you change are written:

```yaml

dsh-ui-font README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml：- id: ui-font
  name: dsh-ui-font
  config:
    sans: '"JetBrains Mono", "BIZ UDPGothic", "Noto Sans JP", sans-serif'
```

The entry id doubles as the settings namespace the browser half reads, so it must stay `ui-font`. Nothing is stored at all until you change a field, and the schema defaults cover a config that omits one:

dsh-ui-font README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml：| Setting | Shipped default |
| --- | --- |
| `sans` | `"JetBrains Mono", "BIZ UDPGothic", "Noto Sans JP", "Yu Gothic UI", Meiryo, sans-serif` |
| `mono` | `"JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", "Fira Code", Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace` |

JetBrains Mono carries no CJK glyphs, so the shipped `sans` falls back to BIZ UDPGothic and Noto Sans JP for Japanese text. Keep at least one CJK-capable family after the Latin font, or Japanese falls back to whatever the browser picks.

dsh-ui-font README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml：A profile can also set the plugin's Loader `config:`, which becomes the base layer under the saved values — see the commented example in `cordis.patch.yml`.

dsh-ui-font README · Repository layout：| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/index.ts` | Host half: declares the two font stacks as volatile config and injects the saved stacks into the served index |
| `src/client.tsx` | Browser half: applies the stylesheet and registers the two settings rows, including the picker |
| `src/shared.ts` | Values shared by both halves: namespace, defaults, sanitising, stack parsing and formatting, and the stylesheet builder |
| `build.ts` | esbuild through tsx on Node.js: host half as ESM, browser half as CJS wrapped in the module-loader format |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Inserts the `ui-font` row into the profile tree |
| `quality.json`, `knip.ts` | Quality gate: the engines `quality-check` runs, all bundled checker rules as errors, warning failures, no baseline exemptions, and the Knip entry points |
| `lib/` | Generated by `pnpm run build` and by `prepack`; not tracked, so it exists only locally and inside the published tarball |
| `tests/host.test.ts`, `tests/client.test.ts`, `tests/shared.test.ts` | Contract tests that run against the built `lib/` |

dsh-ui-font README · How it works：- The host half declares both stacks with `.volatile()`, so the settings domain projects them as an editable entry keyed by the profile row id (`ui-font`). Values are live references: `apply()` reads `config.sans.get()` / `config.mono.get()`, so a write is visible without re-resolving the config.
- The host half calls `settings.configure({ auto: false }, ctx.fiber)` inside `ctx.inject(["settings"], ...)`, because the browser half ships its own row UI and an auto-generated page would duplicate it.
- The host half also pushes one `{ kind: "style" }` row on `webserver/index-inject`. Rows are collected on every index render and placed directly after `<head>`, so the saved stacks are in effect for the first paint, before the browser half has loaded.
- The browser half declares `inject: ["slots", "locale", "configForms"]`, reads the entry with `configForms.get("ui-font")`, and keeps one `style[data-plugin-css="dsh-ui-font/font-family.css"]` tag in sync with the snapshot. Only one authority writes the tokens: both halves emit the same `:root,body{... !important}` declarations, and the tag the browser half appends later wins on equal specificity while the

dsh-ui-font README · How it works：`--dsw-font-mono` is not declared by the stock sheets; some components read it through `var(--dsw-font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace)`, so the override claims it too.

dsh-ui-font README · Development：Use Node.js 22.12.0 or newer and pnpm 10.34.6, as declared in `package.json`. CI uses Node.js 24.

The `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` setting in `package.json` allows only esbuild's dependency build script. Bun 1.4.2 is required only to execute the upstream `quality-check` CLI; dependency installation, builds, and tests use pnpm and Node.js. CI installs Bun solely for that quality gate.

dsh-ui-font README · Development：```powershell
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run check          # tsc --noEmit through @yuu1111/tsconfig/base.json
pnpm run lint           # biome check .
pnpm run format         # biome check --write --unsafe .

dsh-ui-font README · Development：The browser half may only `require()` modules the shell already seeds — `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`. `build.ts` fails the build when any other specifier shows up, and pins the production JSX runtime because the shell does not seed `react/jsx-dev-runtime`.

To try an edit in a live profile without publishing, install this checkout by path and rerun `pnpm run build` after each change:

dsh-ui-font README · Development：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$((Resolve-Path .\dsh-ui-font).Path)"
```

dsh-ui-font README · Release：Bump `version`, commit, then publish a GitHub Release for the matching tag (`v1.1.0` ↔ `1.1.0`). `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds the tarball in a `contents: read` job, verifies the tag against `package.json`, and publishes it from a separate job with npm trusted publishing (`--provenance`), so no long-lived npm token is stored.

dsh-ui-font README · Verified with：- DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings` `0.2.0-rc.2`), Windows 11 / Chromium
- DSH's own plugin compatibility rule accepts this manifest, evaluated with the identical `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })` test `dsh-app-boot` applies to every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer
- `pnpm run test`: module id, exported plugin face, the `configForms` entry read, the settings form policy, the volatile value read, index style row, stylesheet updates, row registration, stack parsing and formatting, the picker paths (installed list, fallback, refused access, free-text add), chip removal and reordering
- `pnpm run check:quality`: Biome, TypeScript, Knip, and the code, comment, document, and TSDoc checkers
